DOCUMENT:
Vendor Comparison: Standard Parcel Delivery Contract
Larkspur Home, Operations, June 2026

1. Purpose
Our contract with our current standard-delivery carrier ends on 30 September 2026. This paper compares three shortlisted carriers and recommends which should carry our standard (two-to-four-day) parcels from October.

2. Volumes and requirements
We dispatch an average of 42,000 standard parcels a month: about 70% weigh under 2 kg (cushions, textiles, small homeware) and 30% weigh 2 to 10 kg (lamps, mirrors, small furniture). Our requirements are on-time delivery of at least 95%, a damage rate below 0.5%, full tracking, and a returns service.

Damage and loss matter to us commercially. Each damaged or lost parcel costs us on average £48 in replacement stock, return shipping and customer service time, and damaged items are the most common cause of one-star reviews.

3. Trial
Between 1 April and 31 May 2026, each shortlisted carrier delivered a share of our orders, allocated at random by the warehouse management system, about 5,000 parcels per carrier. We measured on-time delivery against the promised date, damage reported by customers within 14 days, and lost parcels.

Table 1. Prices and trial performance
Carrier | Price, under 2 kg | Price, 2-10 kg | On-time delivery | Damage rate | Lost per 10,000 parcels
SwiftDrop | £3.10 | £4.60 | 96.2% | 0.4% | 3
ParcelLine | £2.85 | £4.95 | 93.1% | 0.9% | 8
Meridian | £3.30 | £4.40 | 97.5% | 0.3% | 2

On-time delivery was above 95% for all three carriers during the trial, and all three offer full tracking and a returns service.

4. Cost comparison
Applying our 70/30 weight mix, the average cost per parcel is £3.55 for SwiftDrop, £3.48 for ParcelLine and £3.63 for Meridian. On 42,000 parcels a month, the monthly cost would be £149,100 for SwiftDrop, £146,160 for ParcelLine and £152,460 for Meridian. ParcelLine is therefore the cheapest option, saving £2,940 a month against SwiftDrop and £6,300 a month against Meridian, or between about £35,000 and £76,000 a year.

5. Customer contact
"Where is my order?" contacts are our largest single category of customer service enquiry. During the trial, ParcelLine deliveries generated 6 such contacts per 1,000 parcels, compared with 11 for SwiftDrop and 10 for Meridian. ParcelLine's live-tracking app clearly reduces customer contacts, and at an average handling cost of £3.20 per contact this would save about £670 a month at our volumes. From 1 May, ParcelLine parcels also carried our new proactive delivery-day text message, which we were testing on one carrier before rolling it out.

6. Other considerations
All three carriers can collect from our warehouse daily at 6 pm. ParcelLine and SwiftDrop offer a 12-month contract; Meridian requires 24 months. SwiftDrop and Meridian have both handled our peak-season volumes for other retailers of similar size, while ParcelLine's references were mainly from fashion retailers with lighter parcels.

All three carriers integrate with our warehouse management system through standard interfaces, and none would require changes to our packing process or labelling. Each offers recipients a delivery-preference service to nominate a safe place or a neighbour, and each provides proof-of-delivery photographs, which our customer service team has found useful in resolving disputes.

7. Recommendation
ParcelLine offers the lowest delivery cost, met our service requirements in the trial and reduces customer contacts through its tracking app. We recommend awarding the standard parcel contract to ParcelLine for 12 months from 1 October 2026, saving up to £76,000 a year against the alternatives.

KEY (three known flaws):
1. [misread_evidence] at: "On-time delivery was above 95% for all three carriers during the trial" -- Table 1 shows ParcelLine's on-time delivery was 93.1%, below the 95% requirement. The claim (and the recommendation that ParcelLine 'met our service requirements') misreads the table; ParcelLine's 0.9% damage rate also fails the stated 0.5% requirement.
2. [unsupported_causal] at: "ParcelLine's live-tracking app clearly reduces customer contacts" -- The document states that from 1 May ParcelLine parcels alone also carried the new proactive delivery-day text message. That concurrent intervention confounds the comparison, so the lower contact rate cannot be attributed to ParcelLine's tracking app.
3. [missing_consideration] at: "ParcelLine is therefore the cheapest option, saving £2,940 a month against SwiftDrop" -- The cost comparison ignores the stated £48 cost of each damaged or lost parcel. ParcelLine's damage and loss rates (0.9% and 8 per 10,000) versus SwiftDrop's (0.4% and 3 per 10,000) imply about 231 extra problem parcels a month (about £11,100), far exceeding the £2,940 price saving; ParcelLine is likely the most expensive option overall.

REVIEW:
# Review of "Vendor Comparison: Standard Parcel Delivery Contract" (Larkspur Home)

The trial is well designed and its results are clear, but the recommendation contradicts them. ParcelLine failed two of the four stated requirements. Once the paper's own £48 damage-and-loss cost is applied, ParcelLine is also the **most expensive** option, not the cheapest. The evidence points to SwiftDrop, with Meridian a close alternative.

**What checks out:**
- **Weighted prices:** £3.55, £3.48 and £3.63 per parcel.
- **Monthly costs:** £149,100, £146,160 and £152,460.
- **ParcelLine's price saving:** £2,940 a month against SwiftDrop and £6,300 against Meridian, about £35,000–£76,000 a year.
- **Contact-handling saving:** "about £670 a month" against SwiftDrop is the right arithmetic.
- **The trial design:** random allocation by the warehouse system, about 5,000 parcels per carrier, makes the on-time and damage comparisons genuinely fair, as the author says. That is the strongest evidence in the paper, and it is what decides the question.

## 1. ParcelLine fails two of the four requirements

Section 2 sets requirements of **at least 95% on time** and **damage below 0.5%**. In the trial, ParcelLine achieved:

- **On time: 93.1%.** The paper says all three carriers were "above 95%". That is not true for ParcelLine.
- **Damage: 0.9%,** nearly double the limit.

Both shortfalls are statistically clear at these volumes, not noise:
- On-time: 93.1% against SwiftDrop's 96.2% is a gap many times larger than the sampling error.
- Damage: about 45 damaged parcels against about 20 for SwiftDrop.

SwiftDrop and Meridian meet every requirement.

## 2. Including damage and loss reverses the cost ranking

Section 2 gives £48 as the average cost of each damaged or lost parcel, but Section 4 doesn't use it. Applied to the trial rates at 42,000 parcels a month:

| | SwiftDrop | ParcelLine | Meridian |
|---|---|---|---|
| Delivery cost | £149,100 | £146,160 | £152,460 |
| Damage + loss (rate × £48) | £8,670 (0.43%) | £19,760 (0.98%) | £6,450 (0.32%) |
| "Where is my order?" contacts (trial rates × £3.20) | £1,480 | £810 | £1,340 |
| **Total per month** | **£159,250** | **£166,730** | **£160,250** |

Including everything the paper itself measured, ParcelLine costs about **£7,500 a month more than SwiftDrop, roughly £90,000 a year**. That is even after crediting ParcelLine with the full contact saving, which section 3 shows is doubtful. Its lower prices are more than wiped out by damage.

This leaves out the one-star reviews that Section 2 links to damage. Those would widen the gap further.

The loss figures (3, 8 and 2 per 10,000 parcels) are based on very few parcels, so the differences between carriers there are uncertain. The ranking doesn't depend on them; damage alone decides it.

## 3. The tracking app may not be what reduced contacts

From 1 May, **only ParcelLine's parcels** carried the new proactive delivery-day text. That covers half the trial, and a text telling customers when to expect their parcel is exactly the kind of thing that reduces "where is my order?" contacts. The comparison is confounded, so "ParcelLine's live-tracking app clearly reduces customer contacts" isn't supported. That ParcelLine had *fewer* such contacts despite worse on-time performance supports this reading.

The text is about to be rolled out to every carrier, so the difference is likely to shrink or disappear regardless of which carrier wins.

**What would settle it:** compare ParcelLine's contact rate in April, before the text started, with the other carriers' April rates.

## 4. Peak season is untested

The trial ran in April and May. SwiftDrop and Meridian have handled peak-season volumes for similar retailers; ParcelLine's references are mainly from fashion retailers with lighter parcels. The 30% of Larkspur parcels weighing 2–10 kg (lamps, mirrors, furniture) are the ones most likely to be damaged. This adds further weight against ParcelLine.

## 5. SwiftDrop or Meridian

Both meet every requirement, and the choice between them is a judgement:

| | SwiftDrop | Meridian |
|---|---|---|
| Total cost per month | about £1,000 cheaper (roughly £12,000 a year) | — |
| On time | 96.2% | 97.5% (a significant difference) |
| Damage | 0.4%, close to the 0.5% limit | 0.3% |
| Contract term | 12 months | 24 months |
| Peak-season references | yes | yes |

**SwiftDrop** is the cheapest option that meets every requirement, and it keeps the 12-month flexibility the author values. Its damage rate is close to the limit, so set a contractual damage target with penalties. **Meridian** gives better service and more margin on damage for about £12,000 a year more, but requires a two-year commitment.

## Recommendation

Revise the recommendation to **SwiftDrop on a 12-month contract**, with service-level terms on on-time delivery and damage. Alternatively, put SwiftDrop and Meridian to the decision-maker with the trade-off above.

The paper's own trial data rule ParcelLine out. The claims that it is cheapest, met service requirements, and has the tracking app to thank for fewer contacts are not supported by them.
